decisionNote: No final art direction selected. Scores and recommendation are advisory only; Ian chooses.

study.sharedNote: Identical actors, scales, positions, cameras, lights, timings, and events across modes; only the rendering treatment changes. Lade proxy remains a temporary visual placeholder.

performance.notes: Dev-server study scene; render-target count 1 per mode; texture memory not exposed by the harness; shader compile included in loadMs (PMX pipeline dominates 3D modes); zero console/resource errors; mode-switch disposal hook present.

recommendation.label: Agent recommendation (not a decision)
recommendation.reason: Best fit for polished combat, six distinct Dolls, and the full enemy/boss loop: keeps real models, procedural animation, telegraphs, and camera behavior with the lowest production risk. Pixel3d is a close second if a stronger style read or lower GPU cost is wanted. Pixel2d is not advised for a primarily third-person game (rotation popping, sprite-pipeline cost for 6 Dolls plus roster plus bosses).

questionsForIan: Do you prefer readable character detail (cel3d) or a stronger stylized filter (pixel3d) at gameplay distance?
Is 60 FPS minimum acceptable, or must the floor be higher on your target laptop?
Should a future style pass also cover UI/HUD, or 3D rendering only?
Are billboard popping artifacts ever acceptable in third-person, or only top-down?
Which Doll should prove six-Doll scalability after the direction is chosen?

evidence.screenshots: artifacts/screenshots/ad0-<mode>-<view>.png (12 views x 3 modes) plus ad0-normal-no-guide.png and ad0-laser-preview.png

limitations: Pixel2d sprites are code-generated placeholders, not production art and not a proven sprite pipeline.
Study scene is a bounded art study, not the full Grassland stage.
